title: Gold-Indexed Sovereign Bond — Debt Unit of Account and Fiat Settlement Model
status: North Programme economic model / policy design thought experiment; not an existing monetary regime
purpose: Represent a sovereign bond whose principal obligation is indexed to a fixed quantity of gold while settlement may still occur in a fiat currency, so currency dilution does not automatically reduce the real gold-denominated principal owed.
core_distinction: A gold standard disciplines the money by fixing or redeeming the currency against gold. This model instead disciplines the debt: the currency can remain fiat and floating while the debt unit of account is gold-linked.

variables.P0: initial principal in settlement currency at issuance
variables.G0: gold price in settlement currency per unit of gold at issuance
variables.Q: gold quantity defining principal obligation, Q=P0/G0
variables.GT: gold price in settlement currency per unit of gold at maturity T
variables.principal_T: fiat settlement amount of indexed principal at maturity, principal_T=Q*GT
variables.coupon_t: coupon cash flow under the chosen coupon convention

variants.description: Principal is gold-indexed but coupons are fixed in fiat. This protects the principal from currency dilution relative to gold while leaving coupon purchasing power exposed to inflation/depreciation.

Both principal and coupons are defined against the gold-denominated obligation and settled in fiat at the prevailing gold price. This is a stronger creditor-protection design but creates a larger currency/gold mismatch for the issuer.

worked_mechanism.example: If P0=50,000 currency units and G0=500 per gram, the bond represents Q=100 g of gold. If GT=2,000 per gram at maturity, indexed principal settlement becomes 200,000 currency units before any coupon obligation.
worked_mechanism.interpretation: Issuing more currency does not by itself reduce the gold quantity owed. A weaker currency raises the nominal amount required to settle the indexed principal.

what_it_protects: creditor exposure to issuer-currency depreciation relative to gold
principal dilution through ordinary inflation of the settlement unit, to the extent gold preserves the intended reference value
clarity between debt unit of account and settlement medium
what_it_does_not_guarantee: Gold is not identical to a consumer-price index or domestic purchasing power.
Gold prices can be volatile in real-goods terms.
A sovereign can still default, restructure, tax, impose capital controls or change domestic law where legally possible.
Indexation can increase default risk if state revenues remain mostly fiat while debt service rises sharply after currency depreciation.
A fiat coupon can still be inflated away even when principal is gold-indexed.

issuer_balance_sheet_risk.mismatch: Taxes and most public revenues are normally collected in domestic currency while the indexed liability rises when that currency weakens against gold.
issuer_balance_sheet_risk.consequence: The design exchanges part of the creditor's currency-dilution risk for greater fiscal and refinancing risk on the sovereign balance sheet.
issuer_balance_sheet_risk.stress_test: Model debt-service-to-revenue under joint paths for gold price, exchange rate, nominal GDP, tax revenue and interest rates rather than judging the bond from the indexation formula alone.

comparators.main_risk: inflation/currency dilution borne substantially by creditor
designed more directly around domestic purchasing power than gold
currency mismatch between domestic revenues and external debt

comparators.principal_reference: currency itself tied to gold parity/convertibility
comparators.main_risk: monetary system as a whole is constrained rather than only the debt contract

policy_questions: Should indexation apply only to principal or also coupons?
Which gold benchmark, fixing time, currency and settlement convention define Gt?
Should contracts be governed by domestic or external law?
What share of sovereign debt could be indexed before currency/gold mismatch becomes destabilizing?
How does the design compare with CPI-linked debt for the actual policy objective?
Should the government hedge some gold-price exposure or maintain gold-linked reserves/revenues?
north_programme_use: Use as one optional debt-contract design inside the broader European/North obligation graph. It is a model for studying monetary discipline and creditor protection, not a claim that North Programme states should automatically adopt it.
epistemic_status: not a claim of default-proof sovereign debt
